sounds.prompt: A loud 1980s bank burglar alarm bell: a heavy electric gong bell mounted on an outside wall, ringing continuously and fast at a constant rate, hard metallic clanging with a ringing decay between strikes. Steady level from start to end. Recorded outdoors a few metres away, dry, no voice, no music, no siren, no speech.
sounds.reason: Listening criteria (the review pictures, nobody can listen): an even level left to right, a repeating strike pattern (a bell, not a drone), no gap, a loop seam under 5%. All three bank takes open with a ring that dies into 1 to 2 s of silence, then run steady. Take 2 has the clearest steady stretch and a visible strike pattern about every 0.2 s over strong harmonic lines (a struck metal bell), so take 4 is its steady part from 1.8 s on (derive in sounds.json, deriveTake in sound.mjs), 3.1 s, seam 2.7%.

sounds.prompt: A harsh 1980s shop intruder alarm from a wall-mounted box: a piercing electronic buzzing screech in short rapid bursts, on and off about four times a second at one constant pitch, loud and shrill. Steady level from start to end. Recorded indoors close, no voice, no music, no bell, no siren sweep.
sounds.reason: The generator returns one held tone for a pulsed prompt (no take shows on/off in the spectrogram). Take 2 is the most tonal (clean stacked lines, rms flat at -15 dB, no wobble; take 1 is broadband hiss, take 3 wobbles), so take 4 chops it into 130 ms on, 110 ms off, the fast shrill pulsing of a 1980s shop intruder alarm: 20 even bursts, seam 0.0%.

sounds.prompt: A small 1980s corner shop till buzzer alarm: one flat nasal electric buzz from a small plastic box, on for half a second then off for half a second, repeating evenly at a constant level, modest in volume. Recorded indoors in a small room, dry, no voice, no music, no bell, no siren.
sounds.reason: One held buzz again. Take 1 has the flattest level and the lowest seam of the three (5.1%, take 3 24.5%), so take 4 chops it into 500 ms on, 500 ms off: the slow flat buzz of a till buzzer, clearly slower and plainer than the fuel pulses; seam 0.0%.

sounds.prompt: A 1980s armoured van alarm: a loud single-note electric horn honking in short hard blasts, honk, pause, honk, pause, each honk about a third of a second with a third of a second gap, repeating evenly at constant level. Recorded outdoors from a few metres, dry, no voice, no music, no siren sweep, no engine.
sounds.reason: One held horn tone again. Take 1 has the lowest seam (0.8%) and even harmonic lines, so take 4 chops it into 330 ms on, 330 ms off: seven separate honks, an armoured van's horn alarm, a slower honk cadence than the fuel station pulses and a harder note than the store buzz; seam 0.0%.
